text: This classroom project compared the stability of several folded cardboard bridge designs using simple materials and controlled tests. Students built short beam, arch-inspired, and triangular-fold bridges from the same cardboard, keeping length and width as consistent as possible. Each bridge was placed between two supports, and small weights were added gradually to observe bending, tipping, or collapse. The project was limited by handmade construction, a small number of trials, and classroom testing conditions, so the results should not be treated as engineering data. Overall, the triangular-fold designs appeared to hold weight more steadily in this activity, suggesting that fold geometry can influence stability in model bridges.
task: Write a clear abstract for a fictional classroom project comparing the stability of folded cardboard bridges. Describe the method, the limited scope, and a cautious conclusion without claiming real scientific findings.
